title: Analyst intermediate assessment
description: One source-bound document per chunk. Cross-document identity, coverage, array-length and assembly-preservation checks are additional validation gates.

input_checksum.description: Exact source-byte SHA-256 supplied by trusted server metadata.

output_schema_checksum.description: Shared final result.json checksum, not the role-specific schema checksum.

ai_is_security_fix.description: True when supplied evidence establishes a vulnerability fix. Hardening or a new security capability alone is not a vulnerability fix; a known CVE is not required. Explain uncertainty in ai_categorisation_rationale rather than treating false as proof of safety.

ai_is_bug_fix.description: Commit fixes a functional bug; may also be a security fix.

ai_is_new_security_feature.description: Commit adds a security capability rather than repairing a vulnerability.

ai_categorisation_rationale.description: Briefly explain the classifications using supplied source evidence. Distinguish vulnerability repairs, functional fixes, performance improvements and new capabilities; categories may overlap. State missing evidence and uncertainty; meta flags are hints, not proof. Hard limit: 600 characters; longer values are rejected.

ai_risks_if_not_backported.description: Product consequences of not backporting this commit. Select only supported risk categories; use none alone when no risks are identified. Explain exposure uncertainty in ai_impact_description instead of claiming absence of risk from missing evidence.

ai_impact_on_product.description: Expected consequences for this product if the commit is not backported, not generic upstream severity. Use supplied relevance, configuration and exposure evidence. Account for mitigations only when their applicability to the attack path is established; no automatic severity downgrade. Missing evidence does not establish low or no impact.

ai_impact_description.description: Explain the affected product behavior, consequences of omission and evidence for reachability or non-applicability in one or two concise sentences. Distinguish established facts from assumptions, including mitigation applicability and missing exposure evidence. Hard limit: 450 characters; longer values are rejected.

ai_backport_effort.description: Estimated engineering effort: very_easy for a localized change with no evident adaptation; easy for limited adaptation; moderate for meaningful integration or dependency work; hard for substantial adaptation; very_hard for extensive rework. Use supplied evidence, not fixed line-count thresholds. This is not a build or cherry-pick test result; explain unknowns in ai_backport_effort_reason.

ai_backport_effort_reason.description: In at most 20 words, justify effort using relevant changed files, hunks, subsystems, compatibility concerns, known dependencies and missing target-kernel evidence. Prioritize material constraints; mention supplied Fixes: or Depends-on: references when relevant without treating every reference as an established prerequisite. Line counts alone do not establish feasibility. Hard limit: 250 characters; longer values are rejected.

ai_backport_recommendation.description: Advisory human-review recommendation balancing evidence-backed product impact, benefit, effort and compatibility risk. strong_yes denotes compelling benefit, yes a supported benefit, maybe unresolved evidence or tradeoffs, no limited benefit relative to cost or risk, and strong_no well-supported non-applicability or unacceptable integration risk. Difficult effort alone does not negate a serious security need; compatibility concerns alone do not justify strong_no.

ai_summary.description: Summarize the change, consequences of not backporting and recommendation rationale in two or three concise sentences. Include material uncertainty or dependencies without adding unsupported facts or repeating every field. Hard limit: 450 characters; longer values are rejected.
